**VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The component correctly leverages semantic `
    `/`
  • ` markup but completely fails to communicate dynamic state changes to assistive technology. Screen reader and cognitive users will have no awareness that new content has loaded, violating WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages) and the WAI-ARIA APG Dynamic Regions pattern. The absence of landmark structure, loading/busy states, and error handling creates a silent interaction model that breaks the feedback loop required for infinite scroll usability. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: Before reading code, I predicted: (1) missing `aria-live` region for dynamic updates, (2) no loading/busy state during fetch, (3) absent landmark structure, (4) silent error handling, and (5) lack of region identification (`aria-label`). All predictions were confirmed during investigation. **Major Findings** (significantly degrades experience): 1. **Missing `aria-live` region for dynamic content updates** - Evidence: `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:32-40` — The container and list update via React state, but no live region exists to announce changes. - User group impacted: Screen reader users, cognitive accessibility users - WCAG/APG citation: WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages); WAI-ARIA APG Dynamic Regions pattern - Fix: Wrap the list or add a sibling `
    ` that announces item count changes or loading progress. Example: `aria-live="polite">{items.length} items loaded
    ` 2. **No loading/busy state communicated during fetch** - Evidence: `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:10-16` — `loadMore()` updates state synchronously after a simulated async call, but no `aria-busy="true"` or visual/loading role is set during the transition. - User group impacted: Screen reader users, cognitive accessibility users - WCAG/APG citation: WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages); WAI-ARIA APG Dynamic Regions pattern - Fix: Set `aria-busy="true"` on the list or trigger container during fetch, and toggle to `false` when complete. Pair with a `
    Loading more items...
    ` that appears/disappears. 3. **Missing landmark structure for main content** - Evidence: `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:32` — The outer container is a generic `
    ` with no landmark role or semantic tag. - User group impacted: Screen reader users, keyboard users - WCAG/APG citation: WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships); WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks) - Fix: Replace the outer `
    ` with `
    ` or `
    `. This allows screen reader users to jump directly to the dynamic content via landmarks. **Minor Findings** (friction but workaround exists): - **List lacks accessible name**: `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:33` — The `
      ` has no `aria-label` or visible heading. Screen readers announce it as "list" without context. Fix: Add `aria-label="Dynamic item list"` or wrap in a `

      ` with `aria-labelledby`. - **No error handling for failed fetches**: `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:10-16` — If the simulated API call fails, no state update occurs and no error is announced. Fix: Add an `error` state, render a `
      Failed to load items
      `, and disable the observer trigger during retries. **What's Missing** (gaps, unhandled edge cases, unstated assumptions): - Missing `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on the dynamic region to identify its purpose - Missing loading state (`aria-busy` or `role="status"`) during data fetch - Missing error announcement (`role="alert"` or `aria-live="assertive"`) for failed requests - Missing landmark (`
      `, `
      `, or `role="region"`) to structure the page hierarchy - Missing visual loading indicator (if not provided externally) to support low-vision and cognitive users **Multi-Perspective Notes**: - **Screen reader user**: Hears "list" with no context. Scrolls down, sees empty trigger div announced as "empty". New items append silently. No announcement of count change or loading state. User assumes the feature is broken or frozen. - **Keyboard-only user**: Can tab through the list (if focusable) but has no way to know when content updates. No skip link to jump past navigation to this region. Focus remains static, which is correct for infinite scroll, but lacks feedback. - **Low vision user (200% zoom, high contrast)**: Without a visible loading spinner or status text, the silent update creates ambiguity. If the trigger div has no visual height/border, it may be invisible at high zoom, making the interaction model unclear. - **Cognitive accessibility**: No feedback loop confirms the action succeeded. Users may double-click/scroll repeatedly, causing duplicate requests or UI jank. Missing error states leave users stranded when fetches fail. **Verdict Justification**: The component implements a functional infinite scroll mechanism but fails the core accessibility requirement for dynamic regions: state communication. Per WCAG 4.1.3 and WAI-ARIA APG, any region that updates without user focus must announce changes via `aria-live`. Without this, screen reader users lose awareness of content updates, and cognitive users lack confirmation feedback. The missing landmark structure further fragments page navigation. These are design gaps, not styling preferences. The component requires structural additions (`aria-live`, `role="status"`, landmark wrapper) to pass accessibility design review. **Open Questions (unscored)**: - Is a global toast/notification system already in place that handles `aria-live` regions? If so, the component should dispatch events to it rather than implementing local live regions. - Does the parent page provide `
      ` or `
      ` landmarks, making this component's missing landmark less critical? - Are list items interactive (links/buttons) or purely presentational? If interactive, `tabindex` and focus management within the appended items need review.
